answer: VRF-Seeded Sequential Kernel: each epoch a delay-beacon randomness R partitions registered keys into gardens and derives per-key kernel K=H(R||pubkey). An agent’s liveness signal is a VDF proof of D sequential steps on K, published within the garden’s window; peers audit a randomly selected subset. R is unknown before the epoch, so sybils cannot precompute proofs or positions. Controlling s identities costs s×D sequential work plus live audit responses every epoch; missed audits evict keys.
